label: Failing to give the employee a written employment contract: maximum fine
appliesTo: Employers, on every employee including foreign nationals
why: The obligation is widely treated as a formality — the contract is signed, the company keeps it, nobody follows up. It carries a criminal fine, which is the fact that turns 'they never gave me a copy' from an annoyance into something an employee can act on.

history.source: Labor Standards Act, Article 17 and its penalty provision
history.note: Article 17 requires the employer to specify wages, contractual working hours, holidays and annual paid leave, and to deliver the key terms to the employee in writing, electronic documents included. Signing a contract the company then keeps does not satisfy it.
